collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two families have planned a marriage, and one of the pair does not want it: stand by them, or ask them to give it a chance.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (third) and another family have been planning a wedding between (subject) and (friend) for a month. Today, (subject) said, quietly, that (subject.he/she) does not want to marry (friend). (friend) is relieved, as it happens. (third) is mortified. What should happen?

choices.label: Ask Them to Give It a Chance

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (third) goes to the other family and calls the wedding off. It is the most embarrassing day of (third.his/her) life. Then (subject) and (friend) laugh about it together, and become good friends. (third) decides to stop planning weddings.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (third) asks (subject) to spend some time with (friend) first. (subject) does, out of respect. At the end of the month, both of them still say no. The wedding is called off. (third) accepts it, at last.
